events.title: Fed Decision in September?
events.description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent U.S. inflation readings remain above the Federal Reserve’s 2 percent target amid energy price pressures from Middle East supply disruptions, while the August employment report showed solid 162,000 job gains and a steady 4.1 percent unemployment rate. These mixed signals have kept trader consensus nearly even between no change and a 25-basis-point hike at the September 15–16 FOMC meeting, with upcoming CPI data on September 11 positioned to clarify whether price pressures justify tightening or support holding the 3.50–3.75 percent target range. The balanced pricing captures uncertainty over the central bank’s reaction function, as officials have signaled data dependence without clear forward guidance.

eventMetadata.context_description: Elevated inflation readings above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target, driven by energy price pressures and Middle East supply disruptions, combined with a stable labor market featuring unemployment near 4.1–4.3%, have anchored trader consensus around no change at the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. With the federal funds rate held at 3.50–3.75% since late 2025 and new Chair Kevin Warsh emphasizing data dependence over forward guidance, market-implied odds reflect 67.5% probability of holding versus 27.5% for a 25 basis point hike. Recent CPI and PCE prints showing persistent core pressures above 3%, alongside June SEP dots indicating a hawkish tilt among participants, support these probabilities while leaving room for shifts ahead of the September meeting and upcoming employment and inflation releases.
